messages:
dani_oncall: seeing increased packet loss from us-west-2b to our storage backend, GPU attach errors rising from 0.2% -> 4% in the last 10m. svc-health shows degraded launch latencies. opening thread to coordinate a soft evacuation.

sara_ops: ack. what's the current impact on p95 inference latency?

dani_oncall: p95 for large-model routes up ~2200ms (was ~900ms), error budget burn climbing. tail requests timing out when attaching kvstore mounts. non-urgent background jobs (embeddings backfill) are saturated.

dimitri_infra: likely nic-level packet drops on the AZ fabric. i saw similar last month when the leaf switches got microflaps. recommend soft-drain of non-production node pools first, preserve KV caches if possible.

nico_platform: agree. plan: 1) mark non-prod & low-priority dedicated pools in usw2b for soft-evac 2) shift routing weight to usw2a/usw2c via traffic-router 3) spin up burst capacity in usw2a (we have reserved headroom) 4) pre-warm caches and replay hot prefixes to other AZs.

dani_oncall: ok i will start the routing weight change. command: `traffic-router set-weight --region us-west-2 --az us-west-2b=30,us-west-2a=50,us-west-2c=20 --reason "soft-evac us-west-2b link flap"`

oncall-bot: noticed: rate-limit config unchanged. suggest temporarily raise per-tenant concurrent requests for the next 20m to prevent queueing.

sara_ops: running cache pre-warm now. script: `./tools/prefix-replay --src usw2b --dst usw2a,usw2c --top 200` should repopulate KV cache. note: this will increase token cost briefly.

dimitri_infra: i'm tagging the low-priority nodepool with `graceful-drain=true` and launching `kubectl cordon` then `kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force --grace-period=120` for each node. will keep one GPU per rack for warm-up to avoid cold-cache storms.

deploy-bot: drain started on node gpu-usw2b-12 (dani_oncall). status: cordoned -> draining (pods evicted: 16)

maria_sre: if attach errors persist after draining, we'll need to shift serving fallback policy to model-variant small for tail requests to keep latency SLOs. toggle command is `redwood-route update --fallback-variant small --routes a,b,c`

nico_platform: we should also enable automatic kv-cache restore: `redisctl snapshot restore --target usw2a --preserve-ttl` to avoid cold start. double-check kv mounts on pods after evict.

dani_oncall: started weight change and warmup. current router weights: usw2b=30, usw2a=55, usw2c=15. p95 down to ~1.1s for critical routes after warmup but attach errors still around 1.2%.

sara_ops: cost note: spinning on-demand in usw2a will bump short-term monthly OPEX; keeping spots as fallback will lower cost but increased risk. given SLA, approve on-demand burst for up to 2 hours?

dimi_infra: (typo) dimitri_infra: +1 to on-demand; we can move spot nodes to a separate pool with preemptible eviction fallback and rely on routing policy to avoid placing critical flows there.

maria_sre: i'm watching error budget. if we cross 5% global error for >10m escalate to infra pager and open full evac.

dani_oncall: current plan: continue soft-drain of all low-priority pools in usw2b, pre-warm caches, spin on-demand burst in usw2a, shift traffic weights gradually. if attach errors don't drop below 0.5% in 15m, we start hard-evac of remaining pools and launch cross-region spill to us-east-1 as contingency.

oncall-bot: alert suppression: incident INC-20260318-42 muted for non-prod noisy alerts for 40m.

deploy-bot: drain complete on node gpu-usw2b-12. node status: cordoned, pods evicted.

sara_ops: verifying model-serving health across new nodes. small delta in quality for a few prompts due to quantization fallback on smaller variant; raising evaluation alert to track regressions.

dimitri_infra: one thing: ensure disk mounts are remounted with `nfsvers=4.2` on target AZ nodes to reduce attach timeouts — i've seen kernel NFS timeouts exacerbate attach errors.

nico_platform: will update infra-ansible to enforce mount opts and run `ansible-playbook playbooks/remount-nfs.yml --limit usw2a --extra-vars "nfs_version=4.2"`

dani_oncall: 15m check-in: attach errors down to 0.6%, p95 at 980ms. holding on-demand burst for 30 more minutes then scale down if stable. can we capture a quick blameless postmortem afterwards and add a runbook step for leaf switch microflaps?

maria_sre: yes i'll own the postmortem and add runbook entry: "soft-evac sequencing, preserve KV cache, prefilling strategy, routing weight ramp". assign to eng-infra and eng-oncall.

sara_ops: thanks all. i will keep an eye on cost delta and post numbers in #finance-liaison.

dani_oncall: closing thread for now — will update if we need hard-evac. great coordination. :thumbsup:"
